content: Migrant and seasonal agricultural workers, who are predominantly of Latino descent, face an elevated risk of developing type 2 diabetes. This increased risk is attributed to several factors, including persistent food insecurity, which limits access to nutritious and balanced diets essential for maintaining healthy blood sugar levels. Chronic stress can disrupt hormonal balance and contribute to insulin resistance, further exacerbating their vulnerability to diabetes. These workers frequently endure severe poverty, which not only impacts their overall health but also creates significant barriers to accessing adequate healthcare services, including preventive care, diabetes screening, and management resources.
